title: Implement a generic stack in Go
description: Build a LIFO stack in Go using interface{} (any). Tests are injected; implement internal/stack/stack.go to make them pass.

task_spec.prompt:
Create internal/stack/stack.go implementing a LIFO stack of any values.

The package is `stack` and must export:
  func New() *Stack              — create an empty stack
  func (s *Stack) Push(v any)    — push a value onto the top
  func (s *Stack) Pop() (any, bool)  — remove and return top value; false if empty
  func (s *Stack) Peek() (any, bool) — return top value without removing; false if empty
  func (s *Stack) Len() int      — number of elements
  func (s *Stack) IsEmpty() bool — true if no elements

All 6 tests in internal/stack/stack_test.go must pass.
Run: go test ./...
required_artifacts: internal/stack/stack.go with Stack type and New/Push/Pop/Peek/Len/IsEmpty
Pop and Peek return false for empty stack
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
